title: COW-CLM-001: Minimal Functional Fork
question: How much of a mature frozen Granite MoE must become private through copy-on-write expert slices for a real functional mutation to be learned while the parent remains immutable and exactly recoverable?

cell_semantics.activation: one explicit execution ticket selects one complete Cell view
cell_semantics.write: zero-init copy-on-write deltas over selected fused expert slices
cell_semantics.private_delta_dtype: fp32 with cast to parent dtype at execution
cell_semantics.learned_routing: out of scope; COW-CLM-001 uses oracle Cell activation

site_selection.method: rank actual frozen Granite top-k router activations by hit count

capability.task: invented ZOR(a,b)=(2a+3b) mod 10 mapping with deterministic heldout operand pairs

decision.pass_requires: both knowledge and capability tracks have at least one passing capacity in [1,2,4,8] and the minimum passing artifacts verify in fresh model runtimes
decision.private_fraction_policy: report the minimum measured fraction; do not post-hoc add an economic threshold to this protocol

hosted_environment.dual_gpu_policy: knowledge and capability are independent root forks and may run concurrently on cuda:0/cuda:1; one GPU sequential execution remains canonical-valid

nonclaims: COW-CLM-001 does not claim existing Granite experts are Cells.
COW-CLM-001 does not claim arbitrary sibling Cells compose without reconciliation.
COW-CLM-001 does not claim expert-only COW is sufficient for all future capabilities.
COW-CLM-001 does not claim autonomous natural-language Cell routing.
COW-CLM-001 does not rewrite CLM_CONVERSION_KILL_TEST_001, GRANITE_HYBRID_CLM_V0_1, or HYBRID_CLM_PROMPT_ADDRESS_001.
